title: LiteLLM: newer GPT transcription models are sent a format they reject
summary: A worked public case. A LiteLLM proxy user reports that audio transcription with a newer OpenAI model fails because LiteLLM always adds response_format: verbose_json, and asks for a per-model default. Reproducing it shows the per-model default already works through litellm_params, which unblocks the customer today. The real defect is a substring check: only model names containing "gpt-4o" get the GPT transcription config, so every newer gpt-* model inherits Whisper's verbose_json default. A community pull request (#44021) already makes the same fix; I verified it against my reproduction, so the right move is a review, not a second PR.

sources.label: BerriAI/litellm issue #43867: default response format breaks gpt-realtime and is not overwritable (opened 30 Sep 2026, open, no maintainer replies as of 8 Oct)
BerriAI/litellm PR #44021: fix(openai): route gpt-transcribe to GPT audio transcription config (opened 1 Oct 2026 by a community contributor, unmerged as of 8 Oct)
OpenAI API reference: Create transcription (response_format; GPT transcription models accept json or text only)

timeline.note: Case opened from public GitHub issue BerriAI/litellm #43867 (opened 30 Sep 2026; no maintainer replies)

Restated: transcription fails for a newer OpenAI model; the customer's client (OpenWebUI) cannot set response_format per request. Noted that the title says gpt-realtime and the body says gpt-transcribe

Read the source and reproduced against a local stand-in for the OpenAI endpoint: the requested per-model default already works; the cause is a "gpt-4o" substring check that sends every other gpt-* model down the Whisper path
Decision: unblock the customer with a config change now, and investigate as a one-line library fix with a regression test

Before posting, found community PR #44021 (opened 1 Oct) with the same root cause, missed on the first read. Ran the reproduction and the OpenAI transcription tests against its head: all pass. Dropped my own PR in favour of verifying theirs

receive.reporter: LiteLLM proxy user filing publicly on BerriAI/litellm (issue #43867, 30 Sep 2026), running LiteLLM in Docker behind OpenWebUI
receive.environment: LiteLLM 1.103 proxy in Docker; OpenAI provider, model openai/gpt-transcribe; client OpenWebUI, which does not expose response_format
receive.affected: Everyone transcribing through a newer OpenAI GPT model whose name lacks "gpt-4o". Every request fails, so speech-to-text is down for those users, not degraded
receive.evidence: "LiteLLM applies response_format: verbose_json to all audio transcription requests at the transformation layer." Code cited: whisper_transformation.py sets response_format to verbose_json when the key is missing. Requested: a per-model default in the proxy config, a request-level override that wins, and verbose_json as the fallback.
receive.missing: The exact error returned by OpenAI; the full model_list entry; which model the title's "gpt-realtime" refers to, since the body names gpt-transcribe

parse.restated: Transcription requests to a newer OpenAI GPT model are sent response_format: verbose_json, which the model rejects, and the customer's client cannot send a different value per request.
parse.observableFacts:
1. The Whisper transformation adds response_format: verbose_json whenever the request has none.
2. The GPT transformation adds nothing.
3. The requests fail for openai/gpt-transcribe.
4. The client cannot set response_format on each request.
parse.reporterHypothesis: LiteLLM forces verbose_json on all transcription requests and has no way to change the default per model, so a model-level setting is needed.
parse.scope: OpenAI-provider transcription only. Whisper models are correct to get verbose_json, which LiteLLM uses to read the audio duration for cost. gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe are unaffected. Azure is a separate code path.
parse.clarifyingQuestions: What error does OpenAI return? Is the failing model gpt-transcribe, a gpt-realtime model, or both? Has response_format been tried under litellm_params in model_list?

contextualize.recentChanges: None needed to explain it. The selection rule ("gpt-4o" in model) dates from when gpt-4o-transcribe was the only GPT transcription model; models released since do not match it.
contextualize.serviceHealth: Not an outage. OpenAI is enforcing its documented response_format rules for these models; the defect is in what LiteLLM sends.
contextualize.errorTracker: The failure is a 400 from OpenAI naming response_format, which points straight at the request body rather than at LiteLLM or the network.
contextualize.logsAndTraces: Reproduced on main at 29f48e6 against a local HTTP stand-in for the OpenAI endpoint that, like OpenAI, rejects verbose_json for non-Whisper models and records what each request sends. whisper-1: sent verbose_json, OK. gpt-4o-transcribe and gpt-4o-mini-transcribe: sent nothing, OK. gpt-transcribe and gpt-realtime-transcribe: sent verbose_json, 400. Request-level response_format: json: sent json, OK.
contextualize.rumAndReplay: Not applicable: a server-side request translation.
contextualize.patterns: Same failure shape as case 1 in this case library (jobpipe's cisco filter): a substring test that matched the names that existed when it was written and silently excludes the ones that came after.
contextualize.evidenceBundle:
H1. LiteLLM forces verbose_json on every transcription request. Partly true: only on the Whisper config path.
H2. There is no per-model default. Ruled out: a Router built from a model_list entry with response_format: json under litellm_params sends json, and a request-level value still overrides it. All three behaviours the reporter asked for already exist.
H3. The wrong config is selected for the model. Confirmed: ProviderConfigManager.get_provider_audio_transcription_config returns the GPT config only when "gpt-4o" is in the model name, so gpt-transcribe gets the Whisper config and its verbose_json default.
Finding: a config workaround today, and a one-line selection fix for everyone else.

triage.reasoning: The customer is blocked on every transcription, but a supported config setting unblocks them immediately, so this is not an escalation. The underlying defect is small and well located, so it becomes a work ticket with a ready patch rather than a feature request for per-model defaults, which already exist.
triage.whatWouldChangeMyMind: If OpenAI-compatible servers that are not Whisper but still rely on verbose_json (for duration and cost) were common among customers, a name-based rule would be the wrong fix; the selection would need to come from the model cost map instead.

act.actionsTaken:
1. Unblock the customer today: add response_format: json under litellm_params for that model in model_list. Verified on main through the Router, the same path the proxy uses: json is sent and the request succeeds, and a client that does send response_format still overrides it.
2. Reply on the issue: the per-model default they asked for already works this way; the cause is model selection, not a missing setting; and ask which model the title's gpt-realtime refers to.
3. Library fix: PR #44021, opened 1 Oct by a community contributor, already routes OpenAI models starting with "gpt-" and containing "transcribe" to the GPT config. I ran the reproduction against its head (2fd3cf3): whisper-1 still gets verbose_json; gpt-4o-transcribe, gpt-4o-mini-transcribe, gpt-transcribe and gpt-realtime-transcribe get no default and succeed; the litellm_params workaround and request overrides still work; the 38 OpenAI transcription unit tests pass. Recommend merging it rather than opening a second PR.
4. My own version (any "gpt-" model gets the GPT config) is broader and kept as a note on the PR: it would also cover a future GPT audio model without "transcribe" in its name, at the cost of a wider change.
act.deviations: Worked from public sources and a local stand-in for OpenAI, not the live API or the customer's proxy. The proxy itself was not started; the Router path it uses was tested instead. I wrote a fix and regression test before noticing PR #44021, which was already linked on the issue; that patch was not submitted.
act.outcome: Issue #43867 is open with no maintainer replies as of 8 Oct 2026. The customer has a verified workaround, and community PR #44021 fixes the cause, verified against the reproduction; it awaits review.

record.learning: The customer asked for a feature; the problem was a bug. Reproducing what they asked for showed the feature already existed, which turned a roadmap request into a config change today. Rules keyed on model names age with every release: a check for "gpt-4o" was correct the day it was written. And a wrong turn worth keeping: I wrote a fix before checking the issue's Development panel, where a community PR with the same fix had been waiting a week. Check for existing work before writing new work; verifying someone else's fix is often the more useful contribution.
